input.summary:
Done on branch fix/browser-rules (/home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-browser-rules), commit 923a328 on top of 7c5e37e.

1. Shared rules. The scenario rules of browser_evidence now live in one function, `checks.scenario_evidence(report, required, screenshot)`. It collects every problem in report order as (scenario id or None, message): global errors first, then duplicate titles and screenshot-count or screenshot-file problems of passed tests in report order, then NOT_COVERED. `screenshot` is a callback: the verifier's version resolves the file, checks it is inside the output directory and captures it; check-report's version only checks that the file exists. `browser_evidence` raises `BrowserEvidenceError` (a ValueError) with the first problem, so the verifier reports the same first error with the same text as before. The error also carries `scenario_problems`.

2. `python -m workflow check-report <feature-dir or policy.json> <lane> <report.json> [--all]` is wired in workflow/__main__.py. The code is `check_report_main`, `check_report` and `report_policy` in workflow/checks.py. A feature directory's policy is read through launch.load_feature/feature_file. The output is one line per required scenario: `<check>/<id>: ok`, `not in this report`, the verifier's words for the problem, or `browser scenario did not pass`. Then comes a counts line, then `Blocked: ...` with exit 1 or a closing OK line. Scenarios missing from the report fail only with --all. Screenshots must exist but may be anywhere. Run against the live run's candidate report (read-only), it prints `project-workflows-browser/inert-markdown: Expected one screenshot attachment for inert-markdown` and exits 1.

3. Worker-phase gate. `run_lane_commands` gets a new `scenario_errors` list, and it is saved in the packet as `scenario_errors`, each entry prefixed with the check id. `recheck_packet` adds those entries back when their check is deferred. So a passed test's misnamed, missing or duplicated `screenshot:<id>`, or a duplicated scenario title, now blocks the worker phase. Exit status, failing tests, global errors and a report that was never written stay deferred. The candidate phase's reasons are unchanged, and a test asserts the exact three reasons from the live run. Packets saved before this change have no such key and behave as before.

4. Telling the lanes. `guardrails.pinned_task` adds one sentence (BROWSER_RULES) for lanes with a browser check. It states the rules, the Playwright JSON command and `python -m workflow check-report <feature directory or its policy.json> <lane> <tmp>/report.json`. The task template written by `init` (workflow/scaffold.py) gets a browser paragraph with the exact commands (`features/<feature> main`). The operator deletes it for lanes without browser checks, and the TODO count is unchanged. Updated docs: the RUNBOOK (Playwright evidence convention with the worker commands, the worker-phase exception in "Verification policy and evidence", section 1, test coverage), the README (commands table, step 4, Files, Setup) and PRD_PORTABLE_WORKFLOW section 6 (the convention for `(browser)` rows).

The new tests are in workflow/test_browser_rules.py, in three independent classes. `CheckReport` covers a valid report, two wrongly named screenshots (checked against the verifier's own message), a missing attachment or file, a wrong content type, a duplicated title, a failing test, global errors, a partial report with and without --all, a lane without browser checks, an unknown lane, and a feature directory through `python -m workflow`. `WorkerPhaseScenarioEvidence` runs real verification worktrees with a Python stand-in for `playwright test`: a misnamed screenshot blocks the worker phase (also when global errors come first), while no report and a failing test stay deferred. `BrowserRulesInTasks` covers the pinned task and the init template. Red evidence: the module first failed on import; after the check-report step, 4 tests still failed as expected (the pinned sentence, the init template, the `__main__` wiring and the worker-phase block) and passed after the matching changes.

python -m workflow check-report <live run policy.json> ui <live candidate browser-report-2.json> (read-only sanity check)
tests_run.result: exit 1; inert-markdown: Expected one screenshot attachment for inert-markdown, other four scenarios ok, 31 passed

decisions: A duplicated [scenario:<id>] title gates in the worker phase whatever the tests' outcome. It is lane-authored structure that will block the candidate anyway.

Screenshot-file problems of a passed test also count as the lane's own and gate in the worker phase: file missing, outside the output directory, or not a regular file. They are about how the test attaches its evidence.

Worker-phase gating uses a new packet key `scenario_errors` that recheck_packet adds back only for deferred checks. capture_errors and the candidate-phase reasons are unchanged. Packets without the key behave as before.

scenario_evidence collects every problem instead of stopping at the first. The verifier still raises the first, so its message is unchanged. Side effect on blocked browser checks only: screenshots of every passed scenario with a single valid attachment are now captured, even those after the first problem. Before, only screenshots before the first problem were captured.

check-report also fails, with the verifier's wording, on failed tests or no passing tests ('no passing test evidence or failed tests') and on Playwright global errors, since the verifier blocks on those in the candidate phase. It prints the counts per browser check.

check-report on a lane without browser checks, or an unknown lane, exits 1 with 'Blocked: Lane <lane> has no browser check, so it has no scenarios to check' or '<lane> is not a lane of this policy (...)'. I chose exit 1 so a zero exit is never read as 'valid report'.

pinned_task keeps its signature (to avoid conflicts with fix/challenge-resume in repin). So its sentence names the policy as '<feature directory or its policy.json>' instead of an exact path, and uses `python -m workflow` as in the assignment.

New imports in checks.py (argparse, jsonschema ValidationError, validate_policy, launch helpers) are local to the new functions. That keeps the module's import block untouched for fix/worktree-lock merges; launch must be imported locally anyway (circular through pipeline). New tests are in a new module, workflow/test_browser_rules.py, to stay out of files the sibling branches edit.

`init` writes only a unit-check lane, not a browser-lane template. The browser paragraph (rules plus exact commands with features/<feature> main) goes into its single task template under ## Acceptance, marked to delete for lanes without browser checks. It adds no TODO: line.
not_done: The lane-repair relaunch path (third bullet of the issue section) is designed elsewhere, as assigned.

Existing bug, not fixed (guardrails.stop_rule, the challenge-resume agent's file): when ## Stop is the task's last section, stop_rule(pinned task) takes in the 'Approved ownership and checks' JSON, and now also the browser sentence. So the automatic prompt's 'Stop (from your task...)' line repeats them. Confirmed with stop_rule(pinned_task(brief, worker)).

Not run, by instruction: the full suite (python -m workflow.run_tests) and the Playwright-backed classes (workflow.test_pipeline, and the workflow.test_automatic graph classes built on its PipelineTests fixture). They exercise browser_evidence end to end with real Chromium; the integrator runs them.

In the live run the ui lane's worker-phase suite never started (build failed, no report). So the new worker-phase gate alone would not have caught that run; check-report run by the worker, or the pinned sentence and template telling it to, is what would have.
